title: People in my life
cando: describe your family and the people you know

about.text: In this lesson you talk about your family and the people you know. You say who people are and what they are like. You read about the people on a street. Then you describe a person at a station.
goals: Say who people are: That's my uncle, my mother's brother.
Use my, your, his, her, their and 's: Ana's cousin.
Describe people: She's tall and kind. He has glasses.
Read about people on a street, and write about a person you know.
Describe a person so a stranger can find them.

chapters.title: A family photo
chapters.text:
In this lesson you talk about the people in your life.
Ana shows her colleague Omar a family photo.
Omar asks: Who's this? And: What's she like?
What's she like? asks about the person. Is she kind? Is she funny?
Ana answers: That's my uncle. He's tall and kind.
Listen for the family words: parents, grandmother, uncle and cousins.

chapters.title: my, his, her, and Ana's
chapters.text:
Before a person or a thing, say my, your, his, her or their.
For a man, say his: his name. For a woman, say her: her name.
For two people, say their: their house.
To say whose, add 's to a name: Ana's uncle, my mother's brother.
To describe a person, use is or has. She's tall. He has short hair and glasses.
Two describing words? Put and between them. He's tall and kind.

chapters.title: People on my street
chapters.text:
Next, you read about the people on Kwame's street.
There are neighbours, a colleague, a boss, a cat and a dog.
Read it once. Then read it again, slowly, for the details.
Then you write about a person you know.
Say who they are, what they look like and what they are like.

chapters.title: At the station
chapters.text:
Then you meet someone at a station. But where is she?
A station assistant helps you. Describe the person clearly.
She's short. She has grey hair and glasses. She has a red coat.
The assistant asks questions. Answer with she and her.
When the assistant finds her, say thank you.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story about the people in a family.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again and answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: Who is in the photos on your phone?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Many people have photos of their family and friends. In this lesson you talk about them.

conversation.title: A family photo
conversation.setting: It is the lunch break at work. Ana shows her colleague Omar a photo on her phone.
lines: Is that a photo of your family, Ana?
Yes, it's from my birthday. These are my parents.
Who's this, next to your mother?
That's my grandmother. She's eighty, and she's very funny.
And who's the tall man with glasses?
That's my uncle, my mother's brother. He's tall and kind.
Luis. And these two are his daughters, my cousins.
What's she like, the woman with short hair?
That's Marta. She's young and very friendly. She's a nurse.
He isn't in the photo. He's at their house with the dog.
It's a nice photo. Your family looks happy.

questions.q: Who is the tall man with glasses?
questions.why: Ana says: That's my uncle, my mother's brother.
Ana says: She's eighty, and she's very funny.
Ana says: He's at their house with the dog.

phrases.use: Asking about a person in a photo.
Saying who a person is in your family.
Asking what kind of person she is: kind, funny, quiet …
Describing a person with two words.
Saying something kind about a photo.

items.meaning: Your mother and your father.
items.example: My parents live in a village.

items.meaning: The mother of your mother or of your father.
items.example: My grandmother is eighty.

items.meaning: The father of your mother or of your father.
items.example: My grandfather lives with my parents.

items.meaning: The brother of your mother or your father. Also your aunt's husband.
items.example: My uncle Luis is tall and kind.

items.meaning: The sister of your mother or your father. Also your uncle's wife.
items.example: My aunt works in a bank.

items.meaning: The son or daughter of your aunt or uncle.
items.example: My cousin Marta is a nurse.

items.meaning: Not short. High from your feet to your head.
items.example: My brother is very tall.

items.meaning: Not tall. For hair, it means not long.
items.example: He's short, with black hair.

items.meaning: Not old.
items.example: My aunt is young. She's only thirty.

items.meaning: Good to other people. A person like this helps others.
items.example: The nurse is very kind.

items.meaning: Happy to talk to people and to help them.
items.example: Our new neighbour is very friendly.

items.meaning: A person like this makes other people laugh.
items.example: My grandmother is very funny.

items.meaning: It grows on your head. It can be long or short, black, brown or grey.
items.example: She has short black hair.

items.meaning: You wear them on your nose to see better.
items.example: My uncle wears glasses for reading.

sound.title: one book, two books
sound.explain: Two or more: add s. The s has three sounds. After book and cat it is a quiet s. After cousin and dog it is a z sound. After glass and nurse it is a new beat: glass-es. Listen, then say each group.

sayIt.instructions: Say Ana's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Can you hear the s in parents and cousins?
lines: Yes, it's from my birthday. These are my parents.
That's my grandmother. She's eighty, and she's very funny.
That's my uncle, my mother's brother. He's tall and kind.
That's Marta. She's young and very friendly. She's a nurse.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. Look at the words before the people and things.
examples: That's my uncle, my mother's brother.
He's at their house with the dog.
What's she like, the woman with short hair?
spot.question: Who is his here? Who is their? What does my mother's brother mean? Which words describe Marta?
spot.answer: His is the uncle's: his name is Luis. Their is the grandparents': their house. My mother's brother is the brother of my mother: 's says whose. Marta is young and friendly, with short hair.

rules.title: my, your, his, her, their and Ana's
rule: I → my · you → your · he → his · she → her · we → our · they → their
A man: his name. A woman: her name. Two people: their house.
A name + 's: Ana's uncle, my mother's brother, Omar's phone.
His or her? Look at the person, not the thing.
rules.mistake: Not: Omar and her wife. Say: Omar and his wife. Omar is a man.

rules.title: Describing people
rule: is + a describing word: She's tall. They're friendly.
Two words with and: He's tall and kind.
has + hair or glasses: She has short hair. He has glasses.
with: the man with glasses, the woman with short hair.
Ask: What's she like? She's quiet and kind.
rules.mistake: Not: She is short hair. Say: She has short hair.

practice.q: Omar is married. ___ wife is a teacher.
practice.why: Omar is a man, so his.

practice.q: Ana has a brother. ___ brother is a driver.
practice.why: Ana is a woman, so her.

practice.q: My grandparents live in a village. ___ house is small.
The brother of my mother is my ___ brother.
practice.why: Add 's to say whose: my mother's brother.
Hair and glasses go with has: she has short hair.
is + a describing word: he is tall.

practice.q: What's she ___ ? She's quiet and friendly.
practice.why: What's she like? asks what kind of person she is.
the man with glasses: with says what he has.

practice.q: My parents are very ___ . They help everyone.
Is this ___ bag? No, it's Omar's.
practice.why: Before a thing, say your: your bag.

yourTurn.prompt: Think of one person in your family. Write three or four sentences. Say who the person is, what they look like and what they are like.
yourTurn.model: This is my aunt, my father's sister. Her name is Leila. She's short, and she has black hair and glasses. She's very kind and funny.

text.title: People on my street
text.body:
My name is Kwame. I live on Mill Street, and I know a lot of people here.
Mr and Mrs Chen live at number 3. They're old and very quiet. Their cat sits in the window all day.
Next door is Tomasz. He's tall, with short grey hair. He has a big black dog, Max. Every morning they walk to the park.
Priya and Omar live at number 7. Priya is my boss at work, but she's very friendly. Omar is my colleague. We take the bus to the office together.
Carlos works in the café on the corner. He's always happy, and he knows everyone's name.
This week Mrs Chen is sad. Her sister is ill. The people on our street take her food and beautiful flowers.

wrong: a new job in an office
gist.why: Kwame writes about his neighbours and the people on his street.

gist.q: Do the people on the street help each other?
gist.why: They take Mrs Chen food and flowers.

detail.why: Mr and Mrs Chen live at number 3. Their cat sits in the window.
He's tall, with short grey hair.
Kwame says: Priya is my boss at work. Omar is my colleague.
This week Mrs Chen is sad. Her sister is ill.

items.meaning: More than one person: men, women and children.
items.example: There are a lot of people at the station.

items.meaning: A person you work with.
items.example: Omar is my colleague. We work in the same office.

items.meaning: The person at work who tells you what to do.
items.example: My boss is very friendly.

items.meaning: An animal that many people keep at home. You take it for walks.
items.example: Tomasz walks his dog every morning.

items.meaning: A small animal that many people keep at home. It sleeps a lot.
items.example: Their cat sits in the window all day.

items.meaning: Feeling good, often with a smile.
items.example: Carlos is always happy.

items.meaning: Not happy. Feeling bad about something.
items.example: Mrs Chen is sad this week.

items.meaning: Not loud. A person like this does not talk a lot.
items.example: My neighbour is quiet, but very kind.

items.meaning: Very nice to look at.
items.example: The flowers in the café are beautiful.

model.title: My colleague Carlos
model.body:
My colleague Carlos is from Spain.
He's young and tall, and he has short black hair and glasses.
He's very friendly and funny.
We work in the café together.
His wife is a nurse, and they have a beautiful cat.

write.task: Write about a person you know. It can be a neighbour, a colleague or someone in your family. Write four or five sentences, like the model. Say who they are, what they look like and what they are like.
checklist: I said who the person is: my neighbour, my colleague, my aunt …
I said what the person looks like: tall, short, with glasses …
I used his or her one time or more.
I joined two describing words with and: tall and kind.

card.title: At the station
card.situation: Your aunt, Rosa Diaz, arrives on the train from Leeds. The station is very busy, and you can't find her. You ask a station assistant for help.
card.goal: Say who you are meeting. Then describe her: tall or short, her hair, her glasses and her coat.

phrases: Excuse me, can you help me, please?
I'm meeting my aunt, but I can't find her.
She's short, and she has grey hair.
She has glasses and a red coat.
prepare.notes: Choose a person to meet: someone in your family or a colleague. Write four things about them: tall or short, their hair, glasses, and their coat or bag.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher works at the station. Describe the person you are meeting. Your teacher finds them in a picture. Then change roles.
doIt.wehel: You work at a train station. I am meeting a person, but I can't find them. Ask me questions: Is it a man or a woman? Is the person tall or short? What is their hair like? Have they got glasses? Use simple English.

model.title: At the station
lines: Yes, please. I'm meeting my aunt, but I can't find her.
Rosa Diaz. She's on the train from Leeds.
She's short, and she has grey hair.
Yes, she has. And she has a red coat.
Is that her, next to the café? With the big bag?
Yes, that's her! Thank you very much.
compare: Did you say who you are meeting?
Did you say tall or short, and describe her hair?
Did you use she and her, not he and his?
Did you say thank you at the end?

canDo: I can say who the people in a photo are.
I can use my, his, her, their and 's.
I can describe a person: tall, short, kind, with glasses.
I can read about people on a street and write about a person I know.
I can describe a person so a stranger can find them.

reading.before: Look at the title and the pictures. Who are the people? Are they family, friends or colleagues?
reading.talk: Choose one person from the book. What do they look like? What are they like? Write three sentences, or tell Wehel.

quiz.q: The mother of your mother is your ___ .
quiz.why: Your mother's mother is your grandmother.

quiz.q: Mr and Mrs Chen have a cat. ___ cat is black.

quiz.why: The son of your uncle or aunt is your cousin.

quiz.q: The man ___ glasses is my uncle.
quiz.why: the man with glasses: with says what he has.

quiz.q: Priya tells me what to do at work. She's my ___ .
quiz.why: A boss tells people what to do at work.
What's he like? asks what kind of person he is.

quiz.q: Does she live next door? No, she ___ .
quiz.why: The question has does, so the answer has doesn't.
The day, month and year you were born is your date of birth.

liveClass: Day 1: learners show a family photo, or a picture from a magazine, in pairs. They ask: Who's this? What's she like?
Day 2: who is it? One learner describes a person in a picture; the others guess who it is. Use his, her, their and 's.
Day 3: at the station. You are the station assistant. Each learner describes the person they are meeting until you find them; then change roles.
Day 4: talk about the book, answer questions, and let two learners read their writing about a person aloud.
